About this item

  • 12-CUP DURALIFE GLASS CARAFE: The sturdy 12-cup* carafe has measurement markings for accurate filling and an easy-grip handle for comfortable pouring. *Cup equals approximately 5 ounces (varies by brewing technique).
  • SNEAK-A-CUP FEATURE TO PREVENT DRIPS: This feature temporarily stops the flow of coffee so you can pour your first cup before brewing ends without making a mess.
  • EASY-VIEW WATER WINDOW: The front-facing window shows you the exact amount of water that will turn into coffee, and the brew basket requires a standard paper coffee filter for proper operation.
  • DIGITAL CONTROLS WITH RUBBERIZED FEEL: Large, rubberized buttons give you full control of the coffeemaker, and the easy-read screen displays the clock, brew time, and programming options.
  • QUICKTOUCH PROGRAMMING WITH AUTO SHUTOFF: Easily program the 24-hour auto brew feature so you can wake up to a fresh pot of coffee or whenever you desire. 2-Hour Auto Shutoff for added safety and peace of mind with every use.

Product Description

Brew your daily coffee fast with the BLACK+DECKER™ 12-Cup* Programmable Coffeemaker. QuickTouch™ Programming buttons make it easy to set the 24-hour auto brew feature and shave some time off of your morning routine. Other useful features include Sneak-A-Cup™ Technology, the 12-cup* Duralife™ glass carafe, and a washable brew basket. *Cup equals approximately 5 ounces (varies by brewing technique) Black+Decker and the Black+Decker logo are trademarks of The Black & Decker Corporation and are used under license.

    My Mr. Coffee went kaputt a few weeks ago. It just kept powering off, wouldn’t stay on any longer. I originally bought a different coffee pot but it was too cheaply made and not worth saving a few bucks for. I like my traditional grounds coffee and how I make it at home is my favorite way. I drink a cup every morning so having a coffee pot that will hold up matters. I returned it and ordered this Black & Decker. So far I’m very happy with it. It’s sturdy. It seems well-made. There are no leaks and it brews my espresso grounds rather quickly. It’s digital, and you can program it. I can set it for the morning, and it’s ready when I wake up. Makes great tasting coffee. So far, I’ve had it almost a month, and I’m extremely happy with it. Brews up to12 cups and cleans easily, although it doesn’t have a clean option. Keeps coffee nice and hot for about 2 hours, and then automatically shuts off. I have to say, I recommend this coffee pot..

    Measurement is off from real life (1 cup = 5 ounces, not 8), and time buttons are too easy to push
    Reviewed in the United States on August 16, 2026
    Color: BlackStyle: Hot Brew
    Verified Purchase
    Brief content visible, double tap to read full content.
    Full content visible, double tap to read brief content.

    Rating this as a 3 as "okay". I plan on keeping this but here are the things you need to know that I learned within 2 days of having it:

    I bought this coffee maker to replace a single Keurig maker that I have had for over a decade. I began drinking coffee made from fresh ground coffee from a local roaster recently, so using K-cups is out of the question. Also using the K-cup insert for more than one cup is a pain to clear and clean. The Keurig consistently poured 9 ounces at the large setting or 8 ounces for the middle setting, but I always used 1 heaping scoop of beans to one 9 ounces water (and 1/2 ounce of creamer). I then used a separate pour-over drip system to pour the hot water from the Keurig into my cup, which takes 3 or so minutes each cup. My new job is in-office so I needed to brew one "cup" to wake up, and two "cups" to take in a coffee thermos. I have to run the drip system 3 times in order to leave the house. This is why the Black and Decker was necessary. Two coffee systems to make coffee was a pain and even worse for the days I needed to drive into the office.

    First con: As a test I poured two cups (16 ounces) and one cup (8 ounces) into the Karaf to prepare for my use for Monday morning thinking the lack of an ounce would just make my cup a bit peppier. I was annoyed that the measurement on the Keraf (and water reservoir) showed the waterline as being more than "4" -- the water line was just over the top of the painted number 4 which was above the painted line. So in what universe does 24 ounces of water equate to more than 4 units?? It's not equidistant between the 4 and 6 so it doesn't correspond to 5 units. It corresponds to maybe 4.5. So is each unit equal to 5 ounce pours? Well surprisingly that is what Google tells me. Coffee makers use 1 "cup" = 5 ounces, not 8 ounces to leave room for cream. What?? 3 ounces of cream. Gross. So I am measuring 4.8 units for 24 ounces of water according to the Keraf, but logically this should be closer to the midpoint of the 4 and 6 line (ie very close to where "5" would be), but it isn't. If the Keraf or water reservoir stated "4 = 20oz" this at least would make sense. Minus one star for incorrect real-life measurements and propagating this dumb measurement into the 21st century.

    Second con: The benefit of the machine is that you can prepare your water amount with the ground coffee the night before, and set an alarm for it to brew (ie 5:55am) so that when you get up (ie at 6am) the coffee is already brewed. This feature is great. The first thing you need to do is set the actual time by pushing the hour or minute buttons. The con is that you can push these buttons at any point. Ie you don't need to select any other button in order to set the actual time. If you are right handed, the "hour" button is very close to the re-entry of the keraf and any accidental bump to the hour button will move the clock forward. The "Program" button is strictly for the programming of the alarm, not the clock. The Program button should be used as a dual clock setting and "brew alarm" setting. What benefit is it if the machine brews an hour off than the intended time? Minus one star for not designing the button programming to protect the auto-brew setting system time.

    Lastly, this isn't really a specific con, as I have seen this with other coffee brewers...paper filters get easily moved in the brew process resulting in coffee grounds in the keraf. I tested it today with a reusable filter, and no grounds made it into my keraf. I recommend using a reusable filter to ensure no grounds in the coffee (also it's better for the environment).

    TLDR: make sure the time on the clock is correct before you go to bed as you might accidentally bump the time an hour forward. Measure your water from a measuring cup unless your brews are based on a 5 ounce cup measurement.

About this Item

  • 12-CUP DURALIFE GLASS CARAFE: The sturdy 12-cup* carafe has measurement markings for accurate filling and an easy-grip handle for comfortable pouring. *Cup equals approximately 5 ounces (varies by brewing technique).
  • SNEAK-A-CUP FEATURE TO PREVENT DRIPS: This feature temporarily stops the flow of coffee so you can pour your first cup before brewing ends without making a mess.
  • EASY-VIEW WATER WINDOW: The front-facing window shows you the exact amount of water that will turn into coffee, and the brew basket requires a standard paper coffee filter for proper operation.
  • DIGITAL CONTROLS WITH RUBBERIZED FEEL: Large, rubberized buttons give you full control of the coffeemaker, and the easy-read screen displays the clock, brew time, and programming options.
  • QUICKTOUCH PROGRAMMING WITH AUTO SHUTOFF: Easily program the 24-hour auto brew feature so you can wake up to a fresh pot of coffee or whenever you desire. 2-Hour Auto Shutoff for added safety and peace of mind with every use.

Product Description

Brew your daily coffee fast with the BLACK+DECKER™ 12-Cup* Programmable Coffeemaker. QuickTouch™ Programming buttons make it easy to set the 24-hour auto brew feature and shave some time off of your morning routine. Other useful features include Sneak-A-Cup™ Technology, the 12-cup* Duralife™ glass carafe, and a washable brew basket. *Cup equals approximately 5 ounces (varies by brewing technique) Black+Decker and the Black+Decker logo are trademarks of The Black & Decker Corporation and are used under license.
